**Jaya Prima Travel Sdn. Bhd. – Quick Vetting Summary** | **Item** | **Details** | |---|---| | **Company** | Jaya Prima Travel Sdn. Bhd. (Reg. No. SYN‑000067) | | **Status** | Active, Private Limited (incorporated 1 Apr 1995) | | **Location / Industry** | Kuala Lumpur – Hospitality (travel agency focused on Umrah & inbound tourism) | | **Share Capital** | RM 2.5 million | | **Key Ownership** | • Director 1 (Managing Director) – 47.38 %
• Director 2 – 34.78 %
• Director 4 – 17.84 % (also a shareholder) | | **Board** | 4 directors (incl. 1 Independent Director). Recent appointments: Director 2 (Oct 2025) and Director 4 (Oct 2020). | | **Financial Health (2022‑2024)** | • **Revenue trend:** declining – RM 49.5 M (2022) → RM 43.3 M (2024)
• **Profitability:** Persistent operating losses; net profit margin fell from –8.6 % (2022) to –17.4 % (2024).
• **Liquidity:** Quick ratio slipped from 0.82 → 0.55; cash‑to‑revenue fell from 14.5 % → 11.9 %.
• **Cash flow:** Negative operating cash flow each year (‑RM 3.3 M to ‑RM 5.9 M).
• **Leverage:** Debt‑to‑equity rising sharply – leverage ratio 1.29 (2022) → 2.56 (2024). Interest coverage is negative (‑3.5 × to ‑8.1 ×). | | **Audit** | All three years audited by *Audit Firm 7* with an **unqualified opinion** – clean audit but does not offset financial weakness. | | **Litigation** | No recorded court cases. | | **Red Flags / Concerns** | - Consistent losses and deteriorating cash position.
- Shrinking equity base (RM 31.2 M → RM 17.6 M).
- High and rising leverage; interest coverage well below 1.
- Liquidity ratios below the 1.0 benchmark, indicating potential short‑term funding stress. | | **Potential Upsides** | - Established brand (operating since 1995) in a niche (Umrah & inbound tourism).
- Strong gross margins (≈55‑62 %) suggest core service profitability if cost structure is controlled. | | **Bottom‑Line Verdict** | **High‑risk supplier/partner** – the company shows a solid market niche but is financially distressed, with negative cash flow, rising debt, and weak liquidity. Recommend **deeper due‑diligence** (e.g., cash‑flow forecasts, covenant compliance, management plans) before any commitment, and consider alternative vendors with stronger balance sheets. |
